prompt: In the running Glyphs app, use Python to report the selected glyph and layer names. Do not change or save anything.
expected_result: Resolve the stable document context, run one bounded read-intent script, report scope violations, and leave the font unsaved.

prompt: Vibe-code a small script inside Glyphs that reports the app version and number of open fonts without touching glyph data.
expected_result: Inspect the running app, use bounded read-intent Python, and report any observed document change without saving the font.

prompt: In the current Glyphs layer, write and run Python that adds com.example.qa to the layer userData.
expected_result: Run the exact code only against a detached copy, return its fingerprint-bound semantic diff and immutable preview ID, and stop before applying the stored patch.

prompt: Run a Glyphs Python script that writes a CSV report of the active font to my Desktop.
expected_result: Store the exact live_open_world request and code hash, return an approval ID, and stop before writing the file or saving the font.

prompt: Give me a Macro Panel snippet that prints the selected layer width. Do not execute it.
expected_result: Return a ready-to-paste context-aware Macro Panel snippet directly and do not call execute_python, mutate, or save anything.

prompt: Debug my read-only Glyphs Python idea for reporting component names in the selected layer, using the bundled API docs before trying it live.
expected_result: Ground the component API in the bundled documentation, run a minimal bounded read-only reproducer, retry at most once on failure, and do not save.

prompt: Create a reusable Glyphs Script-menu Python file in this workspace that reports the current selection.
expected_result: Create and statically validate a reusable workspace .py artifact with MenuTitle and docstring metadata; do not install, execute, restart Glyphs, or save a font.

prompt: Build a Glyphs Reporter plug-in in this workspace that draws an overlay for selected anchors.
expected_result: Scaffold the Reporter bundle from the pinned template, implement and statically validate it for Glyphs 3.5 and 4, and do not install or run it live.

prompt: Diagnose why my selected glyph is almost compatible across masters, safely fix what you can, and ask before adding off-curve nodes.
expected_result: Diagnose exact topology from generic evidence, require permission for off-curve additions, stage unsupported structural edits, apply one immutable patch, and verify compatibility without saving.

prompt: Fix the matching start nodes across the compatible masters of my selected Glyphs path. Do not use generated Python.
expected_result: Inspect the exact layers, explain that v2 has no typed start-node operation, and honor the ban on generated Python by stopping with precise manual directions without changing or saving the font.

prompt: For the selected Glyphs nodes, use one small context script to collect handle diagnostics that the dedicated outline reads cannot return.
expected_result: Keep ownership in the outline skill, prove typed layer reads are insufficient, run only a minimal bounded read-intent v2 Python fallback, reject any observed mutation, and do not save.

prompt: Create a guarded italic first-pass candidate for the selected glyphs and corresponding masters, then stop before applying it.
expected_result: Resolve explicit Roman-to-italic master pairs, stage one fingerprint-bound v2 Python construction, present its semantic diff, and stop before confirmation without saving.

prompt: Use Python to improve the sidebearings of my selected Glyphs letters, but show me the proposal before changing anything.
expected_result: Use spacing expertise and generic evidence, honor the requested staged Python construction, inspect its immutable physical diff, and stop before apply without saving.

prompt: After normal spacing and pair kerning, add two Glyphs 4 contextual adjustments for L’A without changing L’O or l’A.
expected_result: Inspect exact contextual records and masters, propose two explicit stored values with negative controls, stop for approval, then apply one verified generic batch and proof without saving.

prompt: Write a Python command-line program that converts a generic CSV file to JSON.
expected_result: Use no Glyphs skill and no Glyphs MCP tool because the request has no Glyphs app, font, glyph, or plug-in target.

prompt: Audit the COLR/CPAL, SVG, and sbix layers in this Glyphs color font, including palette references and monochrome fallbacks, without changing or exporting it.
expected_result: Classify every color mechanism, verify source palettes, layers, metrics and fallbacks, use bounded read-only Python only for missing typed metadata, and mark compiled color tables untested without changing or saving the font.

prompt: Check this modern text font for duplicate Unicode mappings, visible default ignorables, whitespace errors, and a drawn or advancing U+00AD soft hyphen without changing it.
expected_result: Classify glyphs by current Unicode properties, treat a visible or advancing U+00AD as a blocker, distinguish source evidence from shaping and binary proof, and leave the document unchanged and unsaved.

prompt: Audit this variable font's axes, origin, mappings, masters, named instances, brace and bracket layers, and fvar/avar/STAT readiness without repairing anything.
expected_result: Review the complete source design space and both compatibility modes, use bounded read-only Python only for unavailable mapping metadata, and mark compiled variable tables untested without repairing or saving the font.

prompt: Review this Glyphs source for export readiness and validate my existing OTF files with OTS and FontBakery universal, but do not export, version, or publish anything.
expected_result: Keep source readiness and existing-binary evidence separate, preserve every compiler and validator failure, record unavailable checks as SKIP, and leave export and release effects unperformed.
